newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour says "budget figures don't add up".
newsitem.headline: UK Labour says "budget figures don't add up".

text.p: Britain's main opposition Labour party on Tuesday accused the Government of trying to suggest spending was going up when it was in fact falling, and said the Government was increasing taxes by an annual net 300 million pounds.

Labour's Alistair Darling, the shadow chief secretary to the Treasury, said: "The Tories are at it again. Their budget figures don't add up. They are trying to create an illusion of increased spending. The reality is different."
Labour aides said their initial calculations of the tax figures had given the 300 million pound figure.
Darling said in a statement figures issued with the budget showed that Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's claims of increased spending on health and education were misleading.

Darling said the figures showed spending on the National Health Service would rise 0.8 percent in 1997/98, but would fall 0.7 percent in real terms the following year. Capital spending had been cut and not matched by the Private Finance Initiative.
"On education, the department's budget is set to fall in real terms by 5.5 percent over the next three years," he said.

"Government targets for spending on education is 73 million pounds less than local authorities are already spending this year. And it is already clear that council taxes could be set to raise by six percent next year," he said.

"Tory promises on health and education spending will not be believed because they will not put more teachers in the classroom, cut NHS bureaucrats or lift the threat hanging over casualty wards. It is proof that no one can trust the Tories.
"The Tories remain the party of high taxation and broken promises. They can't be trusted on tax and spending," he said.
